name: Buttermilk Blue Cheese Dressing
headnote: Daniel Gritzer offers this as a short case for making blue cheese dressing yourself rather than buying it. He builds it on a mild rather than aggressive blue cheese loosened with sour cream and mayonnaise, with lemon juice to bring the whole thing into balance. The point he stresses is the buttermilk, which might look redundant next to two other dairy ingredients but earns its place twice over: it contributes a lactic tang that cuts the richness of the mayonnaise and cheese, and it thins the dressing just enough to pour cleanly over a wedge of iceberg instead of sitting on it in clots.
comment_digest: Two themes dominate this small set of reviews. First, make it ahead: several people report the blue cheese flavor is muted if served right after mixing and that a few hours, or overnight, lets it develop, with one calling it better still on following days. Second, readers consistently want more aromatics than the recipe includes - garlic comes up repeatedly, alongside suggestions of Worcestershire sauce, a dash of cayenne, and using Maytag or gorgonzola in place of a generic mild blue. Consistent with the make-ahead point, the one negative review found the dressing thin, diluted and barely tasting of blue cheese. Greek yogurt was reported as a working substitute for buttermilk where it is unavailable, and it holds a thicker consistency. The dressing is also used as a dip for buffalo wings.
flags: Headnote on this page is very short - only a few sentences plus two 'why it works' bullets, no long article. Page title is 'Best Buttermilk Blue Cheese Dressing Recipe' vs manifest name. Only 12 reviews, several are praise-only.
